forecast.method: Each median is the unit-normalized consensus (ESPN, Sleeper, CBS, FantasyPros and the sportsbook props where posted; FFToday failed this week) times the tier median from the residual library, with the 50 and 90 widths from the tier quantiles. Hand moves stay on probation (closing line value sign agreement 0.489 on 47 moves), so no median leaves its anchor; the one shaped line is Kenneth Walker III, a questionable mixture. The q75-q95 slice fell to 33% (from 35%), so no width change. The pending Keon Coleman claim (for Germie Bernard, Wed 2:00 AM) is not on the roster and is not in these lines.

standing.why: We are #1 at 8-1 (1141.2). End-Zone Dancers (7-2, 1059.5) play Goedel, Escher, Butkus. A win keeps us #1. A loss with an End-Zone Dancers win makes both 8-2, and we stay #1 on Points For unless they outscore us by 81.7 or more this week. No team below them can reach 8-2. So #2 needs a loss and an 82-point gap: about 0.005.

forecast_note: Not in these lines: the pending Keon Coleman claim (WR, Buffalo, for Germie Bernard, Wed 2:00 AM, priority 13 of 13; The Winners and Cutie Mark Crusaders have a WR need and pick ahead). If it lands, Bernard's line is void and Coleman is unforecast. Tool gap found while forecasting: lineup-watch put Bo Nix in for Jayden Daniels at 2:03 AM (d_net +2.1) because Nix had no market line attached, so the engine read his ESPN 20.8 against Daniels' blended 19.7. Daniels leads on every other source (consensus 20.6 against 18.6). The swap is about 2 points in a week where a win is worth 0.3 title points, so no hand move (the watcher would reverse it); the fix (a player with no market line must not keep ESPN alone against a blended rival) waits for an interactive session.
